title: What Two Minutes of Silence Does to Your Body
description:
What do two minutes of silence do to your body? In one lab study, a two-minute pause slowed people's heart rate. Cyto breaks it down from the 6ix for Remembrance Day.

Researchers played music with randomly inserted two-minute pauses and tracked heart rate, blood pressure and breathing. In the pauses, all three dropped, even below where they started (the resting baseline).

Caveat: this was a small lab study (Bernardi 2006, n=24: 12 musicians + 12 non-musicians) using music with pauses. It did not test Remembrance Day ceremonies, so 'your body may go quiet too' is a maybe, not a promise.

Sources (via PubMed):
Bernardi, Porta & Sleight, Heart 2006 — https://doi.org/10.1136/hrt.2005.064600

Lest we forget. Not medical advice.
